stem: Pia's classroom floor plan is a large rectangle $10\,\mathrm{m}$ by $6\,\mathrm{m}$. It is split into Room L and Room R that share a straight side parallel to the $6\,\mathrm{m}$ sides. Room L has area $24\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly finds the width of Room L along the $10\,\mathrm{m}$ side?

options.text: Width $= 24\,\mathrm{m}$, taking the printed area as the width.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Room L uses the shared $6\,\mathrm{m}$ side as one dimension, so width $= \mathrm{area} \div 6 = 24 \div 6 = 4\,\mathrm{m}$.

teacher.key_rationale: In the subdivision, area = length × width with the shared 6 m side. So Room L width is 24÷6=4 m. Taking 24 as a length or multiplying 24×6 ignores that shared-side relation.
